answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a bond before taking jobs, whether surveying a knoll, mapping tundra, or designing a trellis. Payment stays in escrow until a predefined verification test confirms delivery; provable fraud burns the bond. Creating identities is still easy, but using thousands concurrently requires thousands of bonds, tying up the attacker’s capital, while each detected scam destroys real funds rather than just a disposable name.
